name: Jaguar Land Rover
summary: Attack on the UK's largest carmaker halted production for around five weeks across three plants, cascading through more than 5,000 UK organisations. The Cyber Monitoring Centre assessed it as the most economically damaging cyber event in British history and a Category 3 systemic event.

financial.note: CMC modelled GBP 1.9bn UK-wide impact, range 1.6-2.1bn, converted at approximately 1.32. Scenario analysis, not audited accounting.

disruption.note: Production halted about five weeks; full supply-chain recovery ran into January 2026.

novelty.note: First single-company cyber event to cause economic damage on this scale in the UK.

name: Marks & Spencer
summary: Attack on the retailer disrupted online ordering, contactless payment and stock systems for weeks, with customer data taken. Claimed by DragonForce and linked to the Scattered Spider cluster.

disruption.note: Online ordering and some in-store systems disrupted for weeks.

data.note: Customer data confirmed taken.

name: Co-op
summary: Attack on the UK mutual disrupted logistics and left shelves empty in some stores; member data was taken. Part of the same 2025 UK retail campaign as Marks & Spencer.

disruption.note: Logistics and stock systems disrupted for weeks.

data.note: Member data confirmed taken.

name: TRITON / TRISIS
summary: Malware built specifically to manipulate safety instrumented systems at a petrochemical plant - the layer designed to prevent explosions and loss of life. It tripped the plant into shutdown rather than causing physical harm, but its purpose marks a threshold no other incident has crossed.

novelty.note: First malware written to manipulate a safety instrumented system.

disruption.note: Plant tripped to a safe shutdown.

name: Shamoon / Saudi Aramco
summary: Wiper malware destroyed data on around 30,000 workstations at the world's largest oil company, forcing a return to typewriters and fax machines for parts of the business. Production itself was not stopped.

disruption.note: Corporate IT unusable for weeks; oil production itself continued.

novelty.note: Destructive wiper used at scale against a national energy company.

name: Norsk Hydro
summary: LockerGoga ransomware forced one of the world's largest aluminium producers onto manual operation across roughly 50 countries. Hydro refused to pay, published daily updates throughout, and its transparency became the reference model for incident response.

financial.note: NOK 550-650m for the first half of 2019, per Hydro's own quarterly reporting.

disruption.note: Production continued manually; several weeks to restore systems.

novelty.note: Notable for the response model rather than the technique.

name: Synnovis / NHS pathology
summary: Qilin ransomware crippled pathology services for hospitals across south-east London, delaying blood tests, triggering a national O-negative blood shortage and postponing more than 11,000 appointments and procedures. A patient's death was later formally linked to a delayed blood test result.

disruption.note: Services restored by end of 2024; some backlogs persisted far longer.

data.note: Patient data including NHS numbers and test details published.

novelty.note: A patient death formally linked to a ransomware attack - among the first anywhere.

name: British Library
summary: Rhysida ransomware took a national institution's catalogue and digital services offline for months, with staff data published after the library refused to pay. The library then published an unusually candid review of what went wrong.

disruption.note: Catalogue and digital services degraded for months.

data.note: Staff data published after refusal to pay.

name: Royal Mail
summary: LockBit ransomware halted Royal Mail's international export service for weeks, stranding overseas post. The company refused an unusually large ransom demand and the negotiation transcript was later published.

disruption.note: International export services halted for several weeks.

name: Vastaamo
summary: Psychotherapy patients were individually blackmailed with their own session notes after the clinic chain was breached. The company collapsed, and the perpetrator was later convicted - a case defined by the nature of the harm rather than its scale.

data.note: Psychotherapy notes - among the most sensitive categories of personal data.

novelty.note: Individual patients extorted directly with their own clinical records.

name: A.P. Moller-Maersk (NotPetya)
summary: NotPetya destroyed the shipping line's global IT estate, halting terminal operations worldwide and forcing a near-complete rebuild of its network in ten days. Recorded separately from NotPetya itself because the corporate losses were among the largest of any single victim.

financial.note: Company reporting indicated USD 250-300m; upper bound recorded.

disruption.note: Global terminal operations halted; network rebuilt in about ten days.

name: Merck (NotPetya)
summary: NotPetya disrupted manufacturing and research at the pharmaceutical company, producing one of the largest single corporate losses on record and a long insurance dispute over whether an act of war exclusion applied.

financial.note: Loss claimed in insurance litigation; contested for years before settlement.

disruption.note: Manufacturing and research disrupted for weeks.

name: Microsoft Exchange / Hafnium
summary: Four zero-days in Exchange were exploited at scale, first by a state actor and then indiscriminately by others once disclosed, reaching tens of thousands of organisations within days.

novelty.note: Mass exploitation of a zero-day chain immediately after disclosure.

data.note: Mailbox contents accessible across tens of thousands of organisations.

name: Salt Typhoon
summary: A state-linked intrusion reached deep into US telecommunications networks, including systems used for lawful interception - compromising the machinery of surveillance itself.

novelty.note: Compromise of lawful-interception infrastructure.

data.note: Communications metadata and content of high-value targets.

name: Volt Typhoon
summary: A state actor was found living off the land inside critical infrastructure networks with no espionage or disruption observed - positioning for future effect. It is recorded here precisely because conventional impact measures register almost nothing.

novelty.note: Pre-positioning inside critical infrastructure with no observed effect.

disruption.note: No disruption observed - deliberately recorded as zero.

name: Optus
summary: Breach of Australia's second-largest telecoms provider exposed the personal data of around 9.8 million current and former customers, prompting national identity-document reissue and regulatory action.

people.note: Current and former customers; confirm against the regulator's filing.

data.note: Identity documents exposed, prompting national reissue.

name: Kojima Industries / Toyota
summary: An attack on a single plastic-parts supplier stopped Toyota's entire Japanese production - 14 plants and 28 lines - for a day, demonstrating how little slack exists in just-in-time manufacturing.

disruption.note: All Japanese production stopped for one day.

novelty.note: A single small supplier halting a global manufacturer.

name: AIIMS Delhi
summary: Ransomware took India's flagship public hospital offline for weeks, forcing admissions, laboratory and patient records back onto paper across an institution seeing tens of thousands of outpatients.

disruption.note: Core hospital systems offline for weeks; paper fallback.

data.note: Patient records affected; scale not independently confirmed.

name: Albania government
summary: Destructive attacks on Albanian government services led Tirana to sever diplomatic relations with Iran - the first time a cyber attack produced that response from a NATO member.

novelty.note: First cyber attack to result in a NATO member severing diplomatic relations.

disruption.note: Government online services down for an extended period.

name: TransUnion South Africa
summary: Credit bureau breach exposed personal and credit data on a very large share of South African adults, with extortion demands made publicly.

data.note: Credit and identity data; claimed record count not independently confirmed.
